records.name: Parks Canada Discovery Pass
records.summary: Annual Parks Canada pass that covers daily admission at the national parks and historic sites it lists, including Banff, Jasper, Yoho and Kootenay.

season.note: Sold online and at gates and visitor centres; no sale season is stated.

v.note: family or group: up to seven people arriving in one vehicle
admission is free for youth 17 and under

price.quote: Parks Canada Discovery Pass Adult $ 83.50 Senior $ 71.50 Family/Group $ 167.50
price.note: The fees pages give no year; read in the 2026 season. Same prices on the Jasper, Yoho and Kootenay fees pages.

window.note: Buy online before the trip, or at a park gate, information centre or campground.

cancel.note: Non-refundable; signed by the holder, not transferable.

entry.quote: valid for a full 12 months from the date of purchase, expiring on the last day of the month in which it was purchased
entry.note: Hang it from the mirror or put it on the driver side dashboard; the holder must be present. Excludes hot springs, backcountry use, parking and camping.

records.name: Banff National Park daily admission
records.summary: A park pass for each day in the park, bought online, at a gate or at a visitor centre. Youth 17 and under enter free.

season.note: The park is open year-round and the fees page gives no fee season.

v.note: family or group: up to seven people arriving in one vehicle

price.quote: ADMISSION Daily Adult $ 12.25 Senior $ 10.75 Youth free Family/Group $ 24.50
price.note: Read in 2026; admission was free 19 June to 7 September 2026 (Canada Strong Pass) and regular fees apply from 8 September 2026.

window.note: Buy online before the trip, or at a park gate, information centre or campground.

exemptions.note: Through travel without stopping on Highways 1 and 93 South; not on the Icefields or Bow Valley parkways.

entry.quote: Persons travelling without stopping on the Trans-Canada Highway (1) and the Banff-Windermere Highway (93 South)
entry.note: Valid until 16:00 the day after purchase, and in Banff, Jasper, Kootenay, Yoho, Mount Revelstoke, Glacier, Waterton Lakes and Elk Island. A pass is needed for each day of a stay.

records.name: Lake O'Hara day-use bus
records.summary: Reserved return bus up the 11 km road to Lake O'Hara; seats by a spring random draw, then leftovers until 15:30 the day before. Walking is 22 km return.

price.quote: Shuttle - To Lake O'Hara Area and Return Per person $ 25.50
price.note: Plus a reservation fee per booking (3.50 online, 5.50 by phone).

window.quote: you can make a reservation up until 3:30 pm the day prior to your activity date on the bus
window.note: 2026 draw: applications 08:00 2 March to 23:59 23 March MDT, up to six date and time choices; winners have 14 days to claim. That the draw is in March each year is a pattern.

quota.note: Seats per bus are limited; at most six people per reservation, children included.

cancel.note: Less the reservation and cancellation fees; 50% of the bus fare after that. The draw application fee is never refunded.

entry.quote: Maximum 6 people per reservations. Children from 1-16 years old must be included within the reservation.
entry.note: Draw applications are online only; after the draw, reservations online or by phone. The cancellation rule is the general day-use rule of the reservation policies.

records.name: Kananaskis Conservation Pass (day pass)
records.summary: Vehicle pass to park at provincial park and public land sites in Kananaskis Country and the Bow Valley. One pass per vehicle; passengers need none.

season.note: No season is stated; the pass is sold as a day or yearly pass.

price.quote: Personal vehicles Day pass - $15 (registers one vehicle)
price.note: Read in 2026; commercial vehicles pay more.

window.quote: You can purchase your pass up until 11:59 pm on the first day of your visit.
window.note: Cell service is patchy in much of Kananaskis; the page advises buying before arriving.

exemptions.note: Driving through without stopping, or only loading or unloading passengers.
First Nations individuals with status, by an exemption applied for online or in person.
Arriving without a vehicle: on foot, on horseback or by bicycle.

entry.quote: All personal and commercial vehicles parked in parks and public lands in Kananaskis Country and the Bow Valley corridor
entry.note: Passes expire at 23:59 on their last day. Online purchases can be cancelled until 23:59 the day before the pass starts. Camping fees are extra.

records.name: Kananaskis Conservation Pass (yearly pass)
records.summary: Yearly Kananaskis Conservation Pass for up to three vehicles registered at one address; it replaces the day pass for a year from purchase.

v.note: personal vehicles; registers up to three vehicles at one address

window.note: Buy online, by phone or at a Kananaskis visitor information centre.

entry.quote: Annual passes are valid for a full calendar year (365 days) from date of purchase.
entry.note: Vehicles registered to different addresses cannot share one yearly pass.
